models.name: Qwen3.8-27B
models.why: witcheer switched vLLM to the Humming linear backend on a single RTX 5090 with 4-bit NVFP4 Qwen3.8-27B: one request went 56.9 -> 71.6 tok/s (+26% over vLLM's default FP4 kernel); Marlin ties at 75.8 vs 77.1 on a dense int4 27B, and the default FP4 kernel still reads a long prompt fastest. Humming ships inside vLLM 0.32.0 (--linear-backend humming).

engines.hardware: RTX 5090 (single); one request, Humming linear backend
engines.quant: 4-bit NVFP4; Humming kernel vs vLLM default FP4 kernel (56.9 tok/s)

models.name: Qwen3.8-27B (TeksEdge DFlash2 + lookup, RTX 3090)
models.full_name: Qwen3.8-27B on a single RTX 3090: TeksEdge DFlash2 + context lookup + faster verification
models.why: Reported progression on one RTX 3090 24GB: baseline 82 tok/s, optimized MTP 114, DFlash2 + context lookup 138, optimized lookup verification 381 (~4.6x, same GPU and weights); TeksEdge uses blocks of up to 16 tokens with ~15 accepted per block, and a 25,000-token document reproduction went ~260 -> 382 tok/s.

engines.quant: speculative decoding + DFlash2 + context lookup, blocks of up to 16 tokens (~15 accepted/block)

models.name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B
models.full_name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B (Strata on Mac, SSD weight streaming)
models.storage_offload: ~110GB free SSD; shared weights + hottest experts in RAM, the rest streamed from disk
models.why: Slotstream streams the 105GB 4-bit 125B MoE from SSD: 20.9-23.7 tok/s on a 48GB M5 Pro with a 33GB budget, 1.41 tok/s on a Mac mini M2 whose disk reads 1.5 GB/s instead of 17.3 GB/s; a 32k-token prompt on a 16GB Mac is >6 min (author's estimate).

engines.hardware: Mac M5 Pro 48GB unified memory (Apple Silicon), 33GB memory budget; 17.3 GB/s SSD
engines.quant: 4-bit weights (105GB) streamed from SSD; 20.9-23.7 tok/s across short/long/coding prompts

engines.hardware: Mac mini M2 base (Apple Silicon); SSD reads 1.5 GB/s
engines.quant: 4-bit; weights streamed from a slow 1.5 GB/s disk

models.name: Bonsai 2 27B
models.why: Prism ML reports 5.95GB footprints (from ~54GB) and generation speeds of 28 tok/s on an Apple M5 Pro and 120 tok/s on an RTX 5090; it needs a Prism ML-maintained branch of the engine, so it is not a drop-in quant. 84.78 average over 14 thinking-mode benchmarks vs 86.32 for the original Qwen3.8-27B.
